prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 1997 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core pitch
- Build on 1979–97 reforms to keep Britain the “Enterprise Centre of Europe,” combining low taxes, controlled public spending, deregulation, and strong public services. Oppose EU federalism, preserve national sovereignty and the Union, and extend ownership, choice, and opportunity.

Economy and jobs
- Keep public spending growing slower than the economy; aim for government spending under 40% of GDP, balanced budget over the medium term, and a 20p basic income tax rate (top rate capped at 40p).
- Maintain 2.5% inflation target; protect low mortgage rates.
- Reject EU Social Chapter, Working Time Directive, and a national minimum wage; resist new EU employment burdens.
- Support small firms: cut small company corporation tax toward 20p, lighten business rates for small firms, reduce CGT and inheritance tax when prudent, impose “sunset” reviews on regulation, curb late payment.
- Expand trade: complete the Single Market, pursue global tariff-free trade by 2020, new Competition Bill.

Technology and science
- “IT for All,” connect schools, use Millennium Lottery to fund public access to computers; efficient radio spectrum pricing; maintain free, competitive media. Prioritise basic research; encourage applied R&D investment.

Families, ownership, welfare
- Family-focused tax cut: allow transfer of unused personal allowance to a working spouse where there are dependent children/relatives (worth up to £17.50/week).
- Promote saving and share ownership (Share Match); raise inheritance tax threshold over time.
- Major pension reform: new workers to get personal pension funds via NI rebate, with state guarantee of at least current basic pension; older workers unaffected.
- Social services reform: more openness, unified standards public/private, extend direct payments and vouchers, Respite Care Programme for carers.
- Welfare: protect Child Benefit/Family Credit; align lone-parent benefits with two-parent families; intensify anti-fraud; efficiency in administration.

Housing
- Continue Right to Buy; enable commonhold; cut public-sector voids by forcing sale of long-empty properties; boost private renting and public–private regeneration.

Education and skills
- Education Guarantee: national performance targets; publish test results at ages 7, 11, 14 (plus baseline at 5) and marks; tougher English/maths standards; strong discipline and teacher appraisal.
- Expand school autonomy: more grant-maintained powers, greater budget delegation, selection by aptitude, more specialist schools; allow new grammar schools where parents want; keep nursery vouchers; expand Assisted Places; learning credits for 14–21; strengthen NVQs, Modern Apprenticeships.

Health and public services
- Year-on-year real NHS funding increases; expand GP fundholding and primary care; publish outcomes; invest via PFI; more doctors/nurses and training; improve mental health care.
- Extend Citizen’s Charter; widen privatisation/competition: complete rail; privatise London Underground (fare caps) and NATS; expand competition in gas and water; consider Royal Mail options, privatise Parcelforce.
- Limit disruptive strikes in essential services.

Crime, justice, drugs
- More police recruitment; 10,000 CCTV cameras by 1999; voluntary ID card using photo driving licence.
- Tackle youth crime: parental control orders, curfews with electronic tagging, secure training for persistent offenders.
- Mandatory minimum sentences (3 years for persistent burglary; 7 for hard-drug dealing; second serious violent/sexual offence = life); abolish automatic early release; national crime squad; faster justice.
- Strong anti-drugs strategy (enforcement, education, local action).

Environment, countryside, cities
- Regenerate worst estates via tenant-led transfers and private capital (~£25bn over a decade); expand Rough Sleeper Initiative and hostel places.
- Protect green belt; target 60% of new homes on brownfield; rural business support, rate relief for village services; negotiated access not general right to roam; aim to double forest cover.
- Animal welfare leadership in EU; food safety strengthened with independent adviser/council; CAP reform; defend UK fisheries, stop quota hopping.

Europe, world, defence, constitution
- “In Europe, not run by Europe”: keep veto, border controls, budget rebate; oppose Social Chapter and further power shifts to EU; support enlargement and flexible EU.
- Single currency: unlikely safe by 1999; keep option open; any UK entry only after a national referendum.
- Stable defence funding, NATO as cornerstone, rapid deployment capability; no defence review.
- Evolutionary constitutional reform; oppose PR and devolution to Scottish/Welsh assemblies; NI talks based on consent principle.
